page.layout: One page of text in a single column; no marginal notes. The faint fragments at the far left edge belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.

main_text.l: quomodo quoq; Heraclius Heraclij Imperatoris
pater à Philippico ad hostium speculationem emis-
sus, mirificè sit seruatus, deq; Zaberta Persa, & quo-
modo à Chlomarorum oppugnatione destiterint
Romani. adhæc etiam de magna turpiq; fuga Phi-
lippici, turbatoq; ordinc[?] in cducendo[?] exercitu Ro-
mano. ac de morbo qui Philippicum inuaserat. &
quòd Heraclius Heraclij Imperatoris pater curam
ducatus in se susceperit quomodoque in Meridio-
nalem Mediam irruptionem fecerit Romanæ mili-
tiæ subimperator. & ut verno tempore in Persarum
ordines irruerint Romani. Comprehenditur quoq;
libro hoc uti Comentiolus in Abaros expeditione
duxerit, subimperatores habens Marinum & Ca-
ptum. & quam strenuè se habuerint illi contra Aba-
ros, postea vero vivo uterq; captus, quodq; Anfi-
muth duce peditum Romanorum ab Abaris capto
eius postea exercitus per Thraciam excursiones se-
cerit. & Comentioli consultatio an oporteret ad-
riri Abaros, & habita concio super invadendis A-
baris, & concioni isti concio opposita. quomodo
rumor illapsus in exercitum barbarorum, irritum
Comentioli fecerit contra Chaganum consilium.
item de Busa milite, & quomodo dum venarctur
deprehensus sit ab Abaris, & quomodo à 9. man-
ipularibus suis per contemptum neglectus, primus
ideò Abaros obsidionalia instrumenta fabricare
docuerit. & quomodo abs Chagano obsessa Beroe,
conatus non successerit. sic quomodo Diocletian-
i urbem idem ipse obsidens, & in hoc casu fru-
stra fuerit. & quomodo Mauricius Imperator
à communi Byzantiorum vulgo ludibrio habitus,

page.notes: Left edge: fragments of the neighbouring page, left out. Several letters are doubtful at the scan: "ordinc" and "cducendo" (line 6) are unclear; "sit" and "seruatus" were read with long s and may be "fit"/"feruatus" as printed. The ruled marks of the scan (show-through and the edge of the adjacent page) are not transcribed. "Chlomarorum", "Anfimuth" and "Busa" are as far as legible; the printed text "Comentioli" and "Abaris" are kept as printed. Last word "propter" is a catchword at the right foot.
